question: Does a controlled arithmetic interpolation between a bounded counting-sort prompt state and a Numba-compilation prompt state produce a repeatable idea that preserves both techniques?

design.weight_meaning: 0.0 is all A; 1.0 is all B.
design.mixing: Global arithmetic interpolation of corresponding final prompt-conditioned canvas-state positions.

control_gate.A_endpoint: Every weight-0.0 repeat must retain counting sort or bounded frequency counting.
control_gate.B_endpoint: Every weight-1.0 repeat must retain Numba or JIT compilation.
control_gate.failure_behavior: If either endpoint fails, save all endpoint outputs, mark the experiment blocked_controls, and do not spend GPU time on intermediate weights.

hybrid_success_rule: An intermediate output must retain bounded counting/frequency sorting and Numba/JIT compilation in one coherent idea without list.sort or sorted.

interpretation.smooth_transition_with_hybrids: The coordinate may support controlled semantic composition and merits denser confirmation.
interpretation.abrupt_transition_without_hybrids: The coordinate behaves like separate categorical basins rather than a semantic bridge.
interpretation.generic_middle_region: Intermediate states leave both source concepts and project toward unrelated model priors.
interpretation.endpoint_failure: The source controls are unreliable, so intermediate interpolation is not interpretable.

important_limitations: This is a prompt-conditioned final-canvas-state interpolation, not prompt-token averaging or internal-layer injection.
Lexical indicators are a conservative automatic gate and do not replace human review.
This remains an exploratory pilot; confirmatory repetitions and pair selection will be frozen later.
